utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: As a rule, these contents should include -- should be drafted by the security chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Engineering support, applying a certain kind of logic, and you can please respond to that engineering security, I assume that one of the branches would do that but who is in charge of this article?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: The chief of engineering is in charge of that particular item, that would be the head of the engineering arm who is at the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And the morale and psychological preparation of the men for executing the assignment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: That is the assistant commander for morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the last page, in the Serbian version, we have logistics.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Logistics is written by the assistant commander for logistics, with his chiefs of services.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This document is titled, "Command for active combat actions." Can you tell us what type of document this is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: The word itself says, "for active combat action," so this document is part of the combat documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So is this a command document or a document of command?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: According to your recollection, can you tell us what other documents of command are?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Besides these commands that must be written for any combat action or activity, combat documents are also, starting from the top document, a directive, then an order, and then other direct verbal orders that can be issued on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You spent a certain amount of time at the Main Staff. I would like to know if you had an opportunity to get to know command documents, directives.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what kind of a document that is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In principle, a directive.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: A directive is a command document or a document of command, and as the word says itself, it is directive, meaning that it's a document referring to a longer time period and is of a directive nature, and it sets down what would need to be done in a specific time period, which does not mean that this would actually necessarily be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document, P5? This is the directive of the Supreme Commander of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, signed by Mr. Karadzic, the Supreme Commander. Can you please tell us, according to your recollection, of the time when you were at the Main Staff, first of all, tell us, did you have the opportunity to get familiar with this document at the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I did not familiarise myself with this document at the Drina Corps because the corps commander receives it directly, and it's up to him if he would and to what extent he would inform his subordinates about the contents of this directive, so that I did not see the directive at the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When you were at the Main Staff, can you please explain to us the actual procedure of adopting a document like this? Does it have any similarities with the procedure of adopting the order that we discussed or, rather, is this document adopted individually by one person or is this the work, as you said of the previous document, of the entire command?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: This is just like the other combat documents drafted by the commands. It's the result of the group work of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, can we look at 5D361 in e-court now, please. This is your next document, Mr. Lazic. It's a document of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska, of the 31st of March 1995, entitled, "Directive for -- Directive 7/1." Can you please look at page 5 in the Serbian version, item 5.3? I think that it's the same page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you please read 5.3?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not see the English translation on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I'm reading, "Drina Corps, with a persistent defence and active combat activities --"

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you read a bit slower, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: "On the northwestern part of the front and around the enclaves, prevent the breakthrough of the enemy at selected operative tactical axes, and by applying demonstrative action and applying measures of operative tactical masking, link up or engage as strong a force as possible. In joint action with the IBK, implement as soon as possible assignments from operation Spreca 95, in quotes, and in the first stage of the operation, break out on to the line: Vis/Kalesija, and then regroup the forces and in joint cooperation with forces IBK, the 1st Krajina Corps, and the V and the PVO, in the second and third phases of the operation, by applying a suitable manoeuvre, infiltrating stronger groups into the rear of the enemy, and by introducing stronger armoured mechanised forces, execute an attack along the general axes: Kalesija, Dubrave, Tuzla, and break out as soon as possible to the line: Village Serici, Zivinice, Jasicak, Ravno Brdo. And in that way, cut off the forces of the 2nd Corps of the so-called army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, south of the cited line, supported by the -- and the PVO. Forward command post of the corps, pursuant to the corps commander's decision."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, can you please tell me if, in this assignment given to the Drina Corps, the engagement of the Drina Corps is mentioned in any way in relation to Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Evidently, Srebrenica and Zepa are not referred to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If we now go back to that document, 107, the first document that you looked at, and item 2, where your commander, General Zivanovic, refers to directive 7/1, among other things, I'm asking you whether he could have referred to directive 7/1 in view of the content of the assignment of the Drina Corps from directive 7/1.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Looking at the assignment given to the Drina Corps from this directive, there was no need to mention directive 7/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So there was no basis for that in that directive. While you were carrying out your duties as chief of operations and training at the Drina Corps command staff, the Drina Corps staff, you brought in certain documents, you as the chief of the service.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you bring in certain documents?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you mean by bringing in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you write, form, draft, participate in the drafting or conception of certain documents? I'm speaking from the aspect of your profession and your position or the duties that you were performing. Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the first assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Just take it slowly, Colonel. We need to make breaks. Please wait until I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did perform such duties because they are part of my job description.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at document 5D989?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know if this document is in e-court, but we do have hard copies, the English version. So if you agree, we could give you these copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 57, line 17, following the word "directive 7/1" your answer should have been recorded. You said yes. The question was -- so following line 17, answer, "Yes" should be recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The plan of work of the Drina Corps command for the month of December 1994, which was approved by the commander, Major General Milenko Zivanovic and the document was drafted by the Chief of Staff, Colonel Radislav Krstic. Mr. Lazic, do you see on page 1 under item 3, fully close off the Srebrenica enclave, do you see that bit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. These were the priority tasks listed on page 1. These assignments were written on the first page as a rule, to emphasise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If you turn to the following page and look at number 5, under assignment, it says, "Fully close off the Srebrenica enclave."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I can see that. This meant that in that time period, the Srebrenica enclave was not fully closed off or, rather, the defence line had not been set up around Srebrenica and this had to be done in the course of the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If we look at these headlines in the different columns, which says, "Person responsible", the person cooperating on the task or the assignment, the date of commencement, the -- and so on and so forth, can you explain all these elements in relation to the assignment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: The first column says, "Assignment." First we have the ordinal number and then the assignment. Then the person responsible for the assignment because there always had to be the person, the individual, responsible for the execution of the task. In this instance it is the operations and training department. Then, in the column entitled, "Units cooperating," these were the units that were in fact to be physically used to perform the assignment. The time limit for the assignment would define exactly that. And in this particular case, we have the entire month.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was this document drafted in your sector, that's to say in your staff?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the work plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we break, because we are going to break soon. Just for completeness sake, can you explain to us what you have already said, there were no means officer for training and what else? Yes, Mr. Lazic, O and O means what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Operations and training department or sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And who was in charge of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then OBO, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Intelligence support, intelligence organ or intelligence support.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And who was in charge of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And who was the intelligence officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember at this time. I can't remember the name. It was -- or he was a major. He was a reserve officer at any rate. That's why I am less familiar with him. I can't remember the name right now. If I do, I'll let you know. Golic, I believe it was major Golic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And under number 9 we see DK and then NV. What does DK stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the chief of communications of the Drina Corps. Since these were KZ documents, this meant that these were encryption or encrypted documents. That's why it says KZ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue after the break. We'll have a 25-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, under number 14, NS, if you could explain what that NS, supposedly means Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's chief of the traffic service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, it's the document that you were looking at before, this document that was circulated by Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm referring to number 14, drawing up of a plan for the engagement of the KDK in subordinated units. That's what I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Chief of Staff of -- it should be NS and ONO, or rather, there should be a comma after NS but there isn't one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And KDK means what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's encryption documents. KDK. No, no, I apologise. KDK stands for the Drina Corps command in this case, although it's not what you'd call a usual acronym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. OBO, you ever told us what it is, intelligence. I see both, yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, actually on that particular issue I don't know if it was something getting lost in the electronics somewhere but, I think my friends will agree with me, with respect to that particular acronym, OBO, I'm not sure if the witness's answer was recorded correctly or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can put the question again just so the record is clear what OBO indeed stands for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Rather than going back to the transcript to find it. Mr. Lazic, what's OBO, what does OBO stand for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At page 60, lines 7, 8 and 9, he said OBO, intelligence support, intelligence organ or intelligence support. That's what he has answered, page 60, line 7 to 9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you stick to that answer, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. What's PP under section 4, mobilisation and personnel, number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that these acronyms are quite unusual and they were probably used locally. Since this is a draft, probably the author of the draft used these unusual acronyms. Anyway, organ for PP would be the organ for personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I take you to section 5, logistical support, under number 1 and number 2, you see the acronym NOONP, which I'm informed means chief of operations and training. But if it is so, why is this same area or section described as ONO previously in this same document? Are they the same, ONO and OONP, or are they different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are not the same. This refers to the chief of the operations organ in the rear, although I don't believe that such acronyms could have been used. I, for one, would not be able to decipher this OONP. The double O is something I've never come across. But I believe that what it has to do with is the organ for operations in the rear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And while we are still on those two entries, under 1 and 2, section 5, what's POOB?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In which sector, section?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Section 5, where we are the NOONP, section 5, number 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I don't understand. I don't know if I can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think if you can't see it now, it needs to be shown to you. Now you're right, on the screen, you don't have section 5. Yes, yes, yes, you have section 5. Under 1, the second column, okay, I can see it myself, you have a capital P, a small O, and then a capital O and a capital B. You have it under 1 and you have it under 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right. That's short for logistics support or rear support. So that's the term we used for logistics support, PO, logistics; OB, support.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And under number 3, third column, you have NTSI.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] MSAS. That's mines and explosives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. Under 3, the third, NTS and small --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me to explain this fully. We have the acronyms here which relate to the chiefs of technical services. The acronym you referred to was the chief of the technical service. Below that you have the chief of the quartermaster's service. Below that one you have the chief of medical service. And there you have the assistant of the veterinary service, further down. This is what the acronyms in that column stand for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I thank you. I think more or less that is enough. I don't need to know more. I give him back to you, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Let us clarify one more thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The acronym OBO, the OBO of the command, and MUP. Mr. Lazic, do you know if the intelligence and security organ of the Drina Corps in 1991 -- 1994 were one and the same organ?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly if the intelligence and security organ was just one. I only know that there was an intelligence organ and a security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to the concept of command and control, combat training and education. Would that fall within the obligations which were down to the staff and the chief of the operations and training department? In other words, under 1 and 3 respectively?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Obviously, I don't have the document you're referring to in front of me. Can you repeat the title of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, please take the document 5D89 -- or rather, 589.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 989.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Look at the Serb version.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you see the title, "Command and control"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the following page, page 3, you have combat training and education.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Zivanovic, and for the record, we need to go to page 2 of the document in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot see this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The English is circulated. We need to go to page 2, I suppose, of this document. Yes. I think it's on the monitor now. Can you see it now, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On page 1, we have the title, "Command and control." On the following page, under Roman numeral III, combat training and education, have you found that page?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This falls within the remit of the tasks to be carried out by the staff and by the chief of the operations and training department; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do the moral guidance tasks, mobilisation and organisation tasks, logistics support and intelligence and security support fall within the remit of the chiefs and desk officers of these organs of yours? Are they in charge of these?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, for each of these tasks, the persons responsible are the ones that are listed there. For instance, for logistics support, it is the logistics officers or chiefs of respective services who are tasked with them. For security and intelligence, it is the intelligence and security officers respectively who are in charge of them. And this applies to all the rest. As for education and training, it is quite evident on the basis of this plan that only the training of the policemen is being covered here, nothing else. That's why, under column 3, you have the OBO. In other words, the organ for security support.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: After having received these elements, would you then draft the document entitled, "Plan of Drina Corps command work for December of 1994"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you then, after having received elements in this way from all the sectors or combat arms, would you then draft the document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Somebody from the operations sector would put all these elements together and would have put this plan together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And then when the plan is drafted in this way, would you have taken it to the Chief of Staff for his signature and for his inspection?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And then, would the Chief of Staff provide his commander and your commander for that matter for his approval?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is -- it transpires from this document that the commander approves them and the Chief of Staff signs these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can the commander approve or reject any such plan?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the operation that took place in 1994 under the name Krivaja 94? Did Krivaja 94 ever take place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was never carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was the enclave of Srebrenica ever totally enclosed as it has been outlined under task number 5?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I believe that this task was never completed, although there were attempts to enclose the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: We are still on the 1994 plan, the December 1994 plan, and this was supposed to be carried out between the 1st of December and 31st December. My question to you is this: During this period of time, according to your information, was the enclave enclosed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Probably conditions were not put in place that were conducive to the execution of this task. I believe that there were not enough troops or equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that towards the end of that month in 1994, the four-month cease-fire period agreement was signed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Obviously between the two warring sides, the Muslim side and the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: If I may add to that, maybe that's also one of the reasons for which this task was never carried out, was never executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let us just briefly go back to page 4 of this document. You will see that under item number 1 in the logistics support, it says, "Cooperate with HK, standing for the Herzegovina Corps, and SRK, standing for the Sarajevo Romanija Corps." Tell me, please, whether these two corps had anything whatsoever to do with the planning of the enclosing of the enclave of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: It transpires from this plan that all that was envisaged was support or cooperation with the Herzegovina Corps in the organisation and realisation of the logistical support but not in combat terms but in logistic terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, do you know that this operation, Krivaja 94, applies to Srebrenica at all?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this operation. I am not familiar with these plans. I was not involved in any of them. I never saw them actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on to the next document, 5D996. This document is also in e-court and a hard copy version has been provided to the witness. Mr. Lazic, look at the document entitled, "Plan of work of the SPB command for December 1994." SPB Skelani, would that be the independent or autonomous infantry battalion Skelani?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This document was approved on behalf of the commander Lieutenant Colonel Yugoslav Tobus [phoen] and it was drafted by the deputy commander, Captain First Class Zoran Arsovski?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please look at items number 4, 5 and 6. These are certain activities which refer to the enclave of Srebrenica. Under number 4, it says, organisation and carrying out of ambushes on the directions leading from the enclave of Srebrenica to the enclave of Zepa. Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: No. Because this does not involve the operations and training officer. The person in charge was the commander in cooperation with the commander of the sabotage and reconnoitering unit. So we did not have to be abreast of all the activities. Only those who were directly involved in the task had to be aware of such tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of your today's testimony, you spoke about the road leading from Skelani to Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Now could you please look at item number 6, where it says maintenance of the road direction Skelani-Jadar-Jasenova [as interpreted]. Would that be the same road that during that period obviously sometime in December 1994 came under threat?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, we have the previous document 5D989, and this document 5D996. These documents were issued by the superior and subordinate commands, so one of them is a plan of the Drina Corps and the other one is a plan of one of the subordinate units. Tell me, please, if you know, obviously, how were these plans issued? Was there any cooperation in drafting these plans? Do you know anything about how these plans were issued, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: These are monthly plans which arise from the annual plan of work of the command. They are drafted at all levels of command, at all unit levels, from battalion upwards or from the Main Staff down to the autonomous battalions. These are working documents or drafts. They are drafted in the command in order to help the work of the command for that month. All the organs encompassed by the plans participate in their drafting, and the plans are approved by the unit commander. These plans may be submitted to the superior command by the subordinate unit and likewise the superior command may submit those plans to subordinate units in order to provide them with an insight into the planned tasks that lie ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: One more question. This 1994 plan of the Drina Corps which was issued on the 1st of December, and early on you saw directive number 7 which was issued on the 8th of March 1995, which means significantly later after this period when this particular plan was drafted, when this plan of the Drina Corps command was drafted, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes. The directive was issued in March 1995, and has nothing whatsoever to do with this particular plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does this plan refer to the closing off of the enclave of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Please, you have to know that the enclosure as a term refers to the cutting off of the defence line towards Srebrenica because there were interspaces which were not manned and the forces from Srebrenica used those interspaces to leave the enclave and enter the space of Republika Srpska, where they threatened our forces. So enclosure or closing off of the enclave is not a combat activity. It arises from the need to define the troops and the equipment that will cover the areas towards an enclave. In this particular case the enclave is Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Would that imply the physical separation between Zepa and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: No. This does not imply the physical separation, but the physical separation is the result of the enclosing of the line or of linking of the line, defence line, but since the configuration of the terrain on the border between Zepa and Srebrenica, that it makes it almost impossible to take up the whole area, and especially not the valleys and the river courses. So that the forces of the 28th Division always found free interspaces and used those in order to leave the enclave and enter the territory of -- under the control of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic and Mr. Petrusic, please slow down. You've been overlapping and I can sense the difficulties that the interpreters are encountering.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: 5D992 is the following document I would like to show you. This document is in e-court. This is another plan, the plan of work of the Drina Corps command for April 1995, which was drafted by the Chief of Staff, Milenko Lazic, Colonel Milenko Lazic, acting -- standing in for the Chief of Staff, and it was approved by the commander, Milenko Zivanovic. Mr. Lazic, please look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: What's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please look at the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Okay. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On your behalf, somebody else signed the document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Obviously, I wasn't there, so the document was signed by somebody from the operations and training sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the following page, under item 5, a task given to the Drina Corps, "Continue with the operation of completely closing the front line in the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps with the focus on Srebrenica enclave." In the English version, it is on page 2. In the Serbian version, it is also page 2. Yes. That's the page. Let me go back to item 5 which reads, "Continue with the operation to completely close the front line in the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps with a focus around Srebrenica enclave. The person in charge is the operations and training sector," and so on and so forth. Mr. Lazic, tell me, please, when it comes to this task, was it carried out between the 1st of April 1995 and the 30th of April 1995, which was the envisaged period of time according to this plan for the task to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: It is evident from these monthly plans that this task spills over from one month to another, that you have shown me here today, which means that this task was not carried out when it was planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the following plan. So, is this task identical to the December task?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes. In essence, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And did this task follow the directive number 7 in chronological order?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did this plan follow the directive in chronological terms?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes. But it is obvious that the authors of this plan were not aware of the directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, you've told us that you do not -- and correct me if I'm wrong -- fall under the category of persons to whom the directive would have been delivered. Not just you personally but your sector as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. The directive was delivered directly to the commander and as I've already told you, he's the one who then decided how many and to what extent will the people in the corps command be informed about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The plans that we are talking about are approved by the corps commander, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the directive was delivered to the corps commander? I believe that you have told us that it was delivered to the corps commander as well.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I know that from the common practice, from my own practice while I worked in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I would now kindly ask you to go back briefly to the -- to document P5. This is a document accompanying the directive. In some versions it is on the first page and in some versions on the last page. In the English it is on the first page, where you can see the signature of Lieutenant Colonel Manojlo Milovanovic, and I believe that in the Serbian version it is the penultimate page or the last page. Mr. Lazic, you have it on the last page and we have it on the screen. Mr. Lazic, this is a document of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska issued by the Chief of Staff, Lieutenant General Milovanovic and sent to the command of the 1st Krajina Corps, and this document clearly shows that he sent this directive number 7 to the 1st Krajina Corps. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: This is the accompanying document, accompanying the directive which was being sent to the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If we go back to the first page of this document, P5 --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I don't see it on my monitor or -- I can see it now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you see to whom the directive is sent? Is it sent to the 1st or the 2nd Krajina Corps, the Sarajevo Romanija, the Eastern Bosnia, the Herzegovina, the Drina and so on corps? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you able to conclude, even though we don't have such a written document, that the Chief of Staff, Manojlo Milovanovic, sent this document to the command, or rather, to the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I would like to go back to another plan. This is the last plan. 5D995. There is an English version of this document. It's a plan with the same name, "the work of the Drina Corps command for July 1995." Can we look at page 2, please? No, no, sorry. This document has been issued by the Chief of Staff, major Radislav Krstic and it was approved by general corps commander, the corps commander, General Zivanovic. Can we look at page 2 now? Can you look at item 5 again where it says, "Continue with the operation of completely closing the front line in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps with a focus on the Srebrenica enclave"? This is July, and the time when the actual assignment began to be implemented was the 1st of July 1995. Would a characteristic of all the plans that we've seen to date be that the beginning and the end of the action around Srebrenica and the closing of the front line was supposed to last for a month?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: If you're asking me about the duration of the assignment, it was planned to be completed in that month, but it should not -- otherwise, it would need to be regulated with a separate order, the execution of such an assignment, and that would regulate the time period in which that particular assignment would need to be specifically implemented. So it's normal in the monthly plan to have something from the first to the last day of the month but then the regulation of a particular -- implementation of a particular assignment would need to be dealt with in a separate document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So the assignment was supposed to begin at the beginning of July, so were combat actions undertaken in order to close off the Srebrenica area and were any activities of the Drina Corps planned in that period?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Since this is a plan for July 1995, when Srebrenica practically stopped existing as an enclave, it is evident that this plan was drafted before President Karadzic came to the Drina Corps, and the plan did not include President Karadzic's order. What was actually planned in the annual plan was entered into the monthly plan and it's evident that this assignment has remained outstanding and unresolved even though it was planned for several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So could we conclude that the operation Srebrenica was not executed pursuant to this plan?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: It's evident that the order on the implementation of the Srebrenica assignment did not become part of this plan because the plan was completed before the assignment was given for the implementation pertaining to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: We are going to look at a video now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we will look at the video tomorrow, Mr. Petrusic, because our time is up. Yeah, yeah, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know you're tired. And everyone is. But let's continue until 7.00. Let's proceed and we'll finish at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is document 5D1177. Can we please start playing it at 28 minutes and 37 seconds until 29 minutes and 22 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Only a Serbian state can provide tranquillity and happiness to the Serbian people. And second, as far as commanding and functioning of the army is concerned, it will not be any special changes in Supreme Command staff, neither in corps commands. We are very satisfied with the corps commanders. Perhaps we also failed a little too. We wanted to and we created the legend of Mladic because we know that our people want legends. However, we failed to state the success of some other corps commanders. Let's see now. Krstic was planning right in front of me and I commend -- I awarded that task to him for Srebrenica and he did that in an excellent way, of course the Main Staff and Mladic and all the others but we should know that Krstic is a great commander."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you satisfied with that, Mr. Petrusic? There were two problems, one, your client and the other accused couldn't follow in the Serbian language because at least from what I could gather, that was not audible. And the second is, I don't know whether it stopped where you meant it to stop or whether it stopped prematurely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Petrusic. Microphone for Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The video was played before the hearing today. I didn't have any problem with the audio and following the audio. If anyone in the courtroom did have a problem, there is a transcript. We transcribed this segment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure that you're happy with the way it went on. So let's continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, you already talked about this 28th of June, that's already well known, and your meeting with President Karadzic. I played this insert, and I want to ask you if this statement of his given to the television of Republika Srpska at the then programme called Na Braniku Otadzbine [phoen] at the -- defending the homeland, was this interview that President Karadzic gave something that reflects what you said? And that was to plan and execute the operation relating to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, evidently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: During your testimony today, you mentioned operative documents, command documents, supplemental documents. Can you please tell us something about combat reports? What sort of documents are those?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: The word itself, "Combat report," indicates that those documents are combat-type documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So we are talking about reports of the subordinate commands to superior commands, combat reports, regular and interim reports? This is what I asked you about.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that is what I am answering. These are combat documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how a combat report is drafted? Who is responsible for that job? Who is supposed to carry it out? Where does such a document come from? Where does it originate from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Operative commands and strategic level commands such as the Main Staff have -- just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I was going to ask for some clarification about the level of command but the witness began doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Leave it to later. Let him finish first. Go ahead, Mr. Lazic. And if you can cover the point raised by Mr. Thayer as you go along, I think it will be better. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I said that operative level commands, I'm thinking of the corps command, and at the strategic level commands, too, there are operation centres and operational -- or duty shifts. And these operations duty officers are obliged, based on the information about the situation in the unit, to draft combat reports based on particular formats. They are created in the operation centre, certified by the corps commander or the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And what does this form mean, the usual form?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Well, the usual form means that the items are the same, that are written about. You provide information about the enemy. It's similar to a combat order, in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Is it the duty -- well, the Drina Corps had several brigades, let's not mention all of them, five or six, and did those brigades send combat reports to you at the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Based on those reports, did you make reports for your subordinate -- to your superior command?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Based on reports of subordinate units and information available to the corps command, a report is drafted for the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was it the duty of your subordinate units, or any subordinate units, vis-a-vis the superior command, to provide objective and timely reports to the superior command about the situation in their area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, you must pause before you begin your answer. Otherwise we will both be criticised for speaking quickly or for overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. Every military staffer was obliged to report truthfully and timely, and this also applied to the commands. This is one of the basic criteria in commanding, to present facts faithfully and to inform the superior command about this in a timely manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I would like us to look at Exhibit 5D1012.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: 5D1012. You have a hard copy of this document. Yes. We can see it on the screen. Mr. Lazic, this is an information of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska issued by the Chief of Staff, General Manojlo Milovanovic, sent to the commander of the Drina Corps personally. The commander at the time was General Zivanovic. At the time that this document was sent, the 21st of October 1994, were you at the command or the staff of the Drina Corps? Were you at the Drina Corps staff at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that I will be able to deal with this document before we run out of time. So let's not leave it for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, General Milovanovic says in this document, "In view of the fact that the Muslim armed units in the Srebrenica enclave have been continuously carrying out certain preparations for conducting combat operations, which you have also known about for the past 19 months, it was your duty to thwart them in their intentions. You always reported that everything was all right in that enclave. In view of the above, now you must prevent an enemy breakthrough from the Srebrenica enclave at the cost of the survival of the corps command. There will be no pulling back of units from other areas." Mr. Lazic, I would like your comment on this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: It's obvious that the chief of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska wishes to warn the Drina Corps commander about the unrealistic reporting on the situation in Srebrenica, in the Srebrenica enclave. Go ahead, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Is this unrealistic reporting something that could have led to the consequences mentioned by General Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily, because what was done was done. We probably should have closed off the enclaves. It wasn't done, and this is obvious from the monthly plans, for a long period. So the space between the enclaves was used by forces of the 28th Division to communicate between the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Well, we just have one more question and then we are finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the spring of 1995, and even during the time of the signed cease-fire, did you have sabotage or terrorist activities or incursions from the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to stop here for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Lazic. We will continue tomorrow, hopefully finish with your testimony as well. We'll try. We'll do our best. I don't know. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of June, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
